population-synthetic · architecture · real / Sweden

How a Swedish individual is generated

The SCB population generator draws every person one attribute at a time, each conditioned on the attributes already sampled — a conditional chained sampling DAG. This page maps that DAG interactively: which SCB table feeds each attribute, what the sampler conditions on, and — its distinguishing feature — the conditioning each source table supports but the current sampler marginalizes away.

Solid arrows are the conditioning the sampler actually uses. Turn on “Show available-but-unused filters” to reveal the dashed edge where the fetch query omits a breakdown (age) the source table could otherwise provide. Click any node for its table, query, categories and the one-line rationale.

ETL — fetch → parse → distributions

One shared client issues 14 fetch_* calls over 12 SCB tables (families BE, UF, AM, HE, LE, BO); parsers turn each json-stat2 response into probability dicts, assembled into PopulationDistributions, then consumed by SampleService.sample_population.

Per-individual conditional sampling DAG

No population loaded — load a generated SCB population JSON to overlay one individual onto the DAG.
Pick a value on any node (click a node, then choose from its ranked list) and watch downstream distributions recompute. The root (age, sex) keys on age-group.
root (age, sex) causal chain conditional marginal conditioning only if employed age · sex available-but-unused

Click a node (or Tab to it and press Enter) to see its SCB table, PxWeb query, category values, and the conditioning it uses versus the conditioning it leaves on the table.

Candidate SCB tables per output attribute

One block per demographic attribute. Each block lays the candidate SCB source tables side by side (no edges — they are alternatives, not a chain): the table the sampler actually uses, plus any other real SCB table that could produce the same attribute under a different set of filters. Click a table box to inspect its PxWeb query and pick values for the filter categories it conditions on; where the table's distribution is embedded, the sliced output distribution updates live.

Sources. Layout and colour vocabulary ported from scripts/dev/draw_generation_dags.py (sweden_spec() / _base_dag()). Table IDs from src/population_synthetic/generators/real/sweden/constants.py; PxWeb queries from fetch_service.py; conditioning from sample_service.py and parsers.py. Category values from config/mapping/scb/*.json. The available-but-unused filter is derived from the fetch query in fetch_service.py; node rationales from docs/scb_population_distribution_analysis.md. No hardcoded probabilities appear here — only structural identifiers and category labels.
